To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

taurolithocholic acid, a cholestatic bile acid, impaired the hepatic transport and metabolism of sulfobromphthalein in rats by decreasing its excretion from hepatocytes into bile and by increasing its transfer from hepatocytes into the plasma.

taurolithocholic acid impairs the hepatics transport of organic anion by impairing canalular excretion and intra hepatic conjugation as well as by enhancing transfer of organic anions from liver to plasma.

the hepatic transport system for organic anions is impaired in taurolithcholate-induced cholestatis in rats, due to reduced canalicular excretion, increased reflux from the liver to the plasma and reduced conjugation of the dyes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the hepatic transport mechanisms of organic anions.
the mechanisms by which bile acids affect hepatobiliary transport of bile acids and organic anions.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the hepatic transport system for bile salts and other organic anions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cholestatic effect of taurolothocholate is a consequence of the impaired transport of organic anion from the liver to the plasma, and that the impaired transport of bile salt is a secondary event.

taurolithochol-8-sulfate impairs hepatic transport of sulfobromphthalein and other organic anions by decreasing canalicular excretion, increasing sinusoidal reflux and decreasing intrahepatic metabolism.

taurolithocholic acid induced cholestasis is due to a reduction in bile salt excretion, which in turn leads to a reduction in canalicular transport of bile salts, and thus to a reduction in the transport capacity of the canalicular membrane for other organic anions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
taurolithocholic acid impairs canalicular transport of organic anion by decreasing the transport rate of the organic anion and increasing the reflux of organic anions into the plasma.
the bile salt taurolithocholic acid is an excellent tool for studying the hepatic transport system for organic anions in vivo.

taurolithocholic acid induced a cholestasis that could be explained by a combination of a reduced hepatic uptake of organic anions, reduced canalicular excretion, and an increased sinusoidal reflux of organic anions.
